story.iWant: to query the state of my Home Assistant entities (lights, sensors, climate, etc.)
story.soThat: Annie can answer questions about my smart home status like "Is the garage door closed?" or "What's the thermostat set to?"

task.title: Create Home Assistant HTTP Client Base

subtasks.subtask: Implement `HomeAssistantClient` class with httpx async client
Add configuration loading: HA_URL, HA_ACCESS_TOKEN, HA_TIMEOUT
Handle network errors (connection refused, DNS failure)
Implement `get_entities_by_domain(domain: str)` method - GET `/api/states` and filter
Handle "all" domain for complete state dump
Define input schema with oneOf validation (entity_ids OR domain)
Implement tool handler calling appropriate client methods
Format response: status, provider, entities[], query_count
Use pytest-httpx or unittest.mock for mocking HTTP responses

ac.title: Query Specific Entities by ID
ac.when: the `home_assistant_query` tool is called with `entity_ids` parameter
ac.then: the tool returns state, attributes, and last_changed for each entity
ac.testable: Call tool with 2+ entity IDs, verify all entities returned with complete data

ac.title: Query All Entities by Domain
ac.when: the `home_assistant_query` tool is called with `domain` parameter
ac.then: the tool returns all entities in that domain with state, attributes, and last_changed
ac.testable: Call tool with domain="light", verify all light entities returned

ac.title: Handle Entity Not Found (404)
ac.given: an entity ID that doesn't exist in Home Assistant
ac.when: the `home_assistant_query` tool is called with that entity ID
ac.then: the tool returns a graceful error with status="error", error_code="NOT_FOUND"
ac.testable: Call tool with non-existent entity, verify error response format

ac.title: Handle Invalid Token (401)
ac.then: the tool returns status="error", error_code="UNAUTHORIZED" with clear message
ac.testable: Set invalid token, call tool, verify UNAUTHORIZED error

ac.title: Request Timeout Handling
ac.given: Home Assistant takes longer than HA_TIMEOUT seconds to respond
ac.then: the tool returns status="error", error_code="TIMEOUT" after HA_TIMEOUT seconds (default: 10)
ac.testable: Mock slow HA response, verify timeout at configured threshold

ac.title: Structured Logging
ac.then: structured logs include: tool_name, entity_count, duration_ms, status
ac.testable: Check logs for required fields after tool calls

ac.title: Handle Missing Configuration
ac.given: HA_URL or HA_ACCESS_TOKEN is not configured
ac.then: the tool returns status="error", error_code="CONFIG_ERROR" with clear message
ac.testable: Remove HA_URL from env, call tool, verify CONFIG_ERROR

ac.title: Unit Tests with Mocked HA Responses
ac.then: all test cases pass with >90% code coverage using mocked HTTP responses
ac.testable: Run pytest with coverage, verify threshold met

doc.title: Epic 16: Home Assistant Integration
doc.snippet: Implements `home_assistant_query` MCP tool for reading entity states from Home Assistant REST API. Schema, response format, and acceptance criteria defined.

doc.title: Epic 16 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: HomeAssistantClient in mcp_server/tools/home_assistant.py. Data models for EntityState and query responses. REST API endpoints: /api/states and /api/states/{entity_id}.

doc.title: Project Guidelines
doc.snippet: Tools follow JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol. Register in tools.py with schema. Use structured logging with duration_ms for monitoring.

file.reason: Pattern for async HTTP client, error handling (RATE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT, SERVER_ERROR), tool schema with handler, structured logging with duration_ms
Export pattern for new tools. Follow existing structure to add home_assistant_query exports.
Pattern for loading optional API keys, adding to SENSITIVE_VARS for masking. HA_ACCESS_TOKEN should be added to SENSITIVE_VARS in Story 16.4.
Use get_logger(__name__) for structured logging in tool implementation
Testing patterns: AsyncMock for httpx.AsyncClient, patch patterns for config and HTTP calls, test class organization by functionality
Test environment setup, mock fixtures for HTTP client. Add HA_URL and HA_ACCESS_TOKEN to TEST_ENV_VARS.

package.name: httpx
package.note: Already in requirements.txt - async HTTP client for HA REST API

package.name: pytest-asyncio
package.note: Already in requirements.txt - async test support

service.name: Home Assistant
service.note: Must be accessible from Docker network

constraints.constraint: Use httpx.AsyncClient consistent with other MCP tools
HA_ACCESS_TOKEN must be added to SENSITIVE_VARS for log masking (Story 16.4)
Query latency p95 target: less than 500ms
Use structured error responses with status, error_code, error_message fields
All tool calls must log duration_ms for performance monitoring
Minimum 90% code coverage with mocked HTTP responses
Follow existing tool patterns from Epic 15 (web_search, web_crawl)

interface.name: Home Assistant REST API - Get States
interface.notes: Returns all entity states. Requires Bearer token. Filter client-side by domain prefix.

interface.name: Home Assistant REST API - Get State
interface.notes: Returns single entity state. 404 if not found. 401 if invalid token.

interface.name: home_assistant_query Tool Schema
interface.notes: oneOf validation: either entity_ids or domain required. Response includes status, provider, entities[], query_count.

interface.name: EntityState Response Format
interface.signature: { entity_id: str, state: str, attributes: dict, last_changed: str }
interface.notes: Match HA REST API response structure for consistency

interface.name: Error Response Format
interface.signature: { status: "error", provider: "home_assistant", error_code: str, error_message: str, entity_id?: str }
interface.notes: error_code values: NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED, TIMEOUT, CONFIG_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR

tests.standards: Follow pytest patterns from existing MCP tool tests. Use unittest.mock with AsyncMock for httpx.AsyncClient mocking. Organize tests into classes by functionality (TestHomeAssistantClient, TestQueryToolHandler, TestToolSchema). Use conftest.py for shared fixtures. Set SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true in test env to avoid validation on import. Target >90% code coverage.

ideas.idea: test_query_single_entity() - mock GET /api/states/{entity_id}, verify response parsing
test_query_multiple_entities() - mock multiple GETs, verify aggregation
test_query_by_domain_light() - mock GET /api/states, filter light.*, verify count
test_query_by_domain_all() - mock GET /api/states, no filter, return all
test_query_entity_not_found() - mock 404 response, verify NOT_FOUND error
test_query_unauthorized() - mock 401 response, verify UNAUTHORIZED error
test_query_timeout() - mock httpx.TimeoutException, verify TIMEOUT error
test_structured_logging() - capture logs, verify duration_ms, status, entity_count
test_network_error() - mock connection refused, verify NETWORK_ERROR
test_tool_schema_structure() - verify name, description, inputSchema, handler
test_input_schema_one_of() - verify oneOf constraint for entity_ids OR domain
